stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: heavy rain brings Vizag to standstill; civic agencies on high alert
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: heavy rain brings Vizag to standstill; civic agencies on high alert
stories.summary: Fallen trees, waterlogged roads and power interruptions add to disruption; bus services cancelled while beaches remain closed; Visakhapatnam district receives 147.9 mm of rain between 8.30 a.m. and 9 p.m.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A city that seldom slows down was brought to a near halt on Tuesday as Cyclone Arnab drove heavy rain and gusty winds across Visakhapatnam, leaving civic agencies racing to keep roads open and power on.
Schools and anganwadi centres remained closed, 102 bus services were cancelled, and beaches were shut, while residents were advised to stay indoors.
Fallen trees and power interruptions added to the disruption.

According to the Command Control Room, 206 trees came down within the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation limits, and 55 had been cleared by 6 p.m. Of the 103 calls received, 42 related to fallen trees and 51 to power supply; 17 had been attended to.
Rainfall in the district averaged 147.9 mm between 8.30 a.m. and 9 p.m., the highest being 206.8 mm in Gopalapatnam, followed by Visakhapatnam (Rural) at 160.8 mm and Pendurthi at 155.2 mm.
District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore said gusty winds of 40 kmph to 50 kmph had been recorded since morning, and speeds of up to 100 kmph were likely from 9 p.m.
By 6 p.m., 85 people had taken shelter in relief centres opened across the district, and 72 food packets had been distributed, the administration said.
Mr. Kishore said people in vulnerable coastal and hilly habitations had been moved as required.
A National Disaster Response Force team had been deployed, along with 63 earth movers, 30 tree-cutting teams, 50 generators and 75 rescue boats.
The Navy and the Coast Guard were coordinating support.

Mr. Kishore toured Mangamaripeta beach and inspected a relief centre at the Upper GVMC Primary School there, directing officials to ensure drinking water, food, toilets and power, with priority for the elderly, women, children and pregnant women.
At night, he inspected the command control room set up at the Collectorate with Joint Collector G. Vidyadhari and asked for hourly reports.

stories.headline: Election Commision keeps RTI applicant waiting for reply
stories.title: Election Commision keeps RTI applicant waiting for reply
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: EC is yet to respond to an RTI application seeking details of steps taken to address grievances raised by two ECs and copies of files, including notings, related to the issue, despite the 30-day statutory time-limit for giving a reply lapsing, said applicant Commodore Lokesh K Batra (retd) Tuesday.

The application was filed on Sept 25 but the RTI status on EC’s website shows “32 day” and still “in-progress”, Batra said, asking “why EC is maintaining a deafening silence” and “what is EC hiding?” The activist sought copies of the complete set of records of issues and grievances raised by ECs SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.
On Sept 24, in a separate RTI to cabinet secretariat, Batra sought copies of the EC’s communications, details of steps taken and file notings.
He received a response on Oct 19, and documents and file notings on Oct 22.

stories.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for US after election defeat and passport order
stories.title: Flavio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for US after election defeat and passport order
stories.summary: The senator’s departure comes amid a money laundering probe and uncertainty over how he travelled abroad despite a Supreme Court deadline
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday’s presidential election and refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports, two sources said.
The US Embassy in Brazil did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Bolsonaro’s lawyer also did not respond.
It was not immediately clear where Bolsonaro was heading, when he would arrive or whether he would seek asylum.
US President Donald Trump’s administration has previously alleged that Flavio’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.
Flavio’s departure for the United States threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to return them to power.
Reuters reported ahead of Sunday’s election that the US State Department had campaigned to restore them to office.
Bolsonaro was favoured to win Sunday’s presidential election but suffered a shock defeat to leftist Lula.
On Monday, he was given 24 hours to surrender his passports as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing.
That deadline has now passed, and his documents have been cancelled, two other sources said.
It was unclear whether he could enter the United States with his passports cancelled.

stories.headline: Tata Motors’ Iveco takeover offer turns unconditional as shareholding reaches 89%
stories.title: Tata Motors’ Iveco takeover offer turns unconditional as shareholding reaches 89%
stories.summary: Tata Motors’ offer for Iveco Group has become unconditional after 238.16 million shares were tendered, taking its subsidiary’s holding to 89.42% of Iveco’s common share capital, net of treasury shares. The final results confirm that the threshold and all other conditions of the offer have been met.

stories.headline: India could have achieved over 8% GDP growth without external shocks: RBI Deputy Governor
stories.title: India could have achieved over 8% GDP growth without external shocks: RBI Deputy Governor
stories.summary: Poonam Gupta highlighted domestic investment, foreign capital and economic resilience as key factors shaping India’s growth prospects amid global uncertainty.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Reserve Bank Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta on Tuesday said the country’s real GDP growth would have exceeded 8 per cent but for the external shocks over the last three years.

Underlining that India has grown at over 7 per cent in an “inconducive environment”, Gupta said that if and when the external environment gets better, up to 1 percentage point will immediately be added to the country’s growth.

Speaking at the annual Business Standard BFSI Insight Summit here, Gupta recalled that we began our journey of growth acceleration with the 1991 economic reforms, and added that a lot of work has gone into various aspects over the years, including strengthening the systems, putting a digital infrastructure in place, states becoming important partners in growth, among others.
“Just based on the strength of that work, we would have already been an 8 per cent growth economy,” Gupta, who handled the monetary policy department at the central bank, said.
“If the global environment gets better, another 50 bps to 1 percentage point growth will come just from there,” she added.

Acknowledging that driving growth is not easy, Gupta said a lot of factors need to be internalised to accelerate the growth, including learning from other countries, upping domestic investments and securing foreign direct investment.
In the current environment, she said the fuel and external finance remain a challenge confronting us, and sounded more confident about food despite the impact of the El Nino.
“Food is not a challenge; if anything, we are becoming an exporter.
This year is El Nino, but even then it is managed very well,” she said.

She said the fiscal policy can help cushion the initial impact of supply shocks through targeted supply-side measures, but they need to be consistent with continued fiscal prudence and overall macroeconomic stability.

“Due to constant policy actions and adaptation, the economy has become less sensitive to some of the shocks that used to impact the economy much more in the past, whether it is the volume of oil used, deficiency in rainfall, etc,” she added.
Not relying excessively on a single stream of economic activity has also proved to be advantageous for India, she said.
